role: Marketing programme manager; international relations manager
description: According to LSM's and TV3's profiles, his professional career began at Lattelecom, where he managed marketing programmes and worked in international relations. The sources consulted do not give the dates.

role: Managing director (SIA Auto Torino); regional head (SIA Auto Group Baltic)
organization: SIA Auto Torino; SIA Auto Group Baltic (car dealers)
description: After Lattelecom he moved to the car trade, as managing director (rīkotājdirektors) of Auto Torino and regional head of Auto Group Baltic (LSM, TV3). The sources consulted do not give the dates.

role: Regional head in Latvia; board member of group companies
description: According to the LETA biography published by Apollo, he worked at Inchcape Motors Latvia from 2008 to 2013 as its regional head in Latvia and sat on the boards of SIA Latvijas pilnvaroto autotirgotāju centrs, SIA Baltic Motors Ventspils, SIA BM Līzings, SIA Ventmotors, SIA Inchcape BM Auto, SIA Inchcape Insurance Services, SIA Ērmans and SIA Baltijas īpašumu fonds, and of the Latvian association of car-body repairers. LSM describes him as having headed the Inchcape group of car-distribution companies in Latvia.
The LETA biography published by Apollo states that from 2013 to 2022 he was regional and development manager at GeesinkNorba in the Netherlands. Other profiles consulted do not mention this post.

role: Board member, then chairman of the board (president)
organization: Auto Asociācija (Latvian Automobile Association, the association of authorised car dealers)
description: He has held various leadership posts in the association since 2006 (LETA) and was listed as chairman of its board in his 2022 and 2024 candidate data and in the declaration he filed as an MP in 2022. TV3 still described him as the association's president in May 2026; the sources consulted do not say whether he stepped down on becoming Prime Minister.

organization: Saeima of the Republic of Latvia
description: Elected in October 2022 on the United List ticket as a non-party member, representing the association 'Apvienotais Latvijas saraksts' founded by businessman Uldis Pīlēns. He sat in opposition, chaired the Innovation Ecosystem Development Subcommittee and served on the Committee on National Economy, Agrarian, Environmental and Regional Policy and the Public Expenditure and Audit Committee. TV3 notes that he voted against advancing the Climate Law and against changes to the vehicle operation tax, the road user charge and a solidarity payment for fuel traders. Like the other United List ministers, he gave up his seat to a substitute on joining the government on 28 May 2026.

role: Chairman, parliamentary inquiry committee on Rail Baltica
organization: Saeima of the Republic of Latvia
description: Chaired the Saeima's parliamentary inquiry committee into the problems and cost overruns of the Rail Baltica railway. Its final report, presented in December 2024, found that the Transport Ministry had concealed the true cost increase from the Cabinet, named 18 people it held responsible — singling out former Prime Minister Krišjānis Kariņš, Transport Minister Kaspars Briškens and former minister Tālis Linkaits — and made 16 proposals; only opposition MPs supported it.

role: Chairman, parliamentary inquiry committee on Riga's district-heating costs
organization: Saeima of the Republic of Latvia
description: The Saeima set up the committee on 6 November 2025, for six months, to examine the causes of the rise in Riga's district-heating prices and related energy-security risks. As chairman, Kulbergs said in January 2026 that he suspected mismanagement and waste of money in the system, citing heat released unused by Latvenergo; Latvenergo and the Public Utilities Commission rejected the criticism, and committee member Kaspars Briškens (Progressives) urged waiting for independent expertise. LSM described him as still chairing it in May 2026, when he became Prime Minister.

role: Leader of the association 'Latvijas restarts' (formerly 'Apvienotais Latvijas saraksts')
organization: Latvijas restarts (association within the United List)
description: LSM reported in May 2026 that the association founded by Uldis Pīlēns, which he represented on the United List ticket, had been renamed 'Latvijas restarts' and that Kulbergs had taken over its leadership from Pīlēns; he has not joined any party, saying party membership is not a prerequisite for standing for election or holding office. The exact date he took over is not given in the sources consulted.

organization: Cabinet of Ministers of the Republic of Latvia
description: Nominated by President Edgars Rinkēvičs on 16 May 2026 after Evika Siliņa's resignation, he formed within two weeks a coalition of the United List, the National Alliance, New Unity and the Union of Greens and Farmers, approved by the Saeima on 28 May by 66 votes to 25, with five ministers continuing from the Siliņa government and only two women among 15 cabinet members. The Union of Greens and Farmers left the Saeima at the 3 October 2026 election. As of 23 October 2026 his cabinet remains in office with full powers; the President announced on 6 October that he would entrust Kulbergs with forming the next government, a statement of political rather than legal force, since the formal nomination can come only after the new Saeima convenes on 3 November and the current government resigns. Coalition talks with the National Alliance and New Unity were scheduled for 28 October.
